strategy: Replaced the 256-iteration per-expert python loop (2 .item() D2H syncs + 1 slice-assign launch per expert) with a fully vectorized align: scatter_add_ counts (avoids bincount's hidden max() sync), a single stacked cumsum over stack((padded,counts)), fused base=(cum_padded-padded)-(cum_counts-counts) so dest=base[flat][order]+iota needs one gather, one scatter_ into a pad-filled buffer, and bucketize(iota_blocks, cum_padded//block_m, right=True, out_int32=True) for expert_ids. Removed the last host sync by sizing buffers from the static host bound EM_max=ceil_bm(numel+min(E,numel)*(block_m-1)) and keeping num_tokens_post_padded on device (tail blocks measured free: 2.960 vs 2.965 ms). Then captured the ~20 remaining tiny align dispatches into a CUDA graph keyed only by (numel, block_m, num_experts, device, dtype) with real topk_ids copy_'d into the static input every call. Also torch.zeros -> torch.empty for out.
strategies_tried: P0-ALG: vectorized moe_align_block_size (scatter_add counts + cumsum offsets + stable argsort + single scatter_), removing all 512 per-expert .item() host syncs and 256 slice-assign launches -> geomean 2.823x
P4-LAUNCH: static host-side EM_max upper bound for sorted_token_ids/expert_ids, num_tokens_post_padded kept as a device tensor, grid over EM_max (verified tail blocks cost ~0.005 ms)
P4-LAUNCH: dispatch collapse inside align - stacked cumsum (2 prefix sums, 1 dispatch), fused base[] so one gather instead of two, bucketize with out_int32 to drop a cast -> align 0.225 -> 0.199 ms
P4-LAUNCH: shape-keyed CUDA graph capture of the whole align step -> align 0.199 -> 0.076-0.129 ms, geomean 2.823x -> 2.914x
W0: torch.zeros -> torch.empty for the out buffer (every valid row fully written, pad rows masked) - real but small (~3.5 us)
notes: The per-expert python loop was the entire story: 6.9-12.7 ms of flat cost that scaled with E=256 rather than with tokens, which is why the smallest case gained most (3.43x on case0 vs 2.65x on case3). Isolated align-only timing, old -> vectorized -> +graph: case0 7.62 -> 0.205 -> 0.076 ms; case1 9.80 -> 0.198 -> 0.096; case2 11.83 -> 0.199 -> 0.109; case3 12.67 -> 0.199 -> 0.129. That is ~100x on the align term and beats the assigned stretch target (<0.1 ms) on cases 0-1. Two findings worth carrying forward: (1) torch.bincount hides a device->host sync in its max() - scatter_add_ into a zeros(E) is the sync-free equivalent; (2) once every op in a host-side prologue is <10 us, the dispatch count IS the cost and only CUDA-graph capture removes it - the last 0.12 ms of the win came purely from graph replay, not from any further op fusion. Oversizing the output buffers to a static EM_max is genuinely free: measured EM_max vs tight-EM grids at 2.960 vs 2.965 ms (case0) and 7.220 vs 7.232 ms (case3), i.e. the extra tail blocks are within noise because the kernel's pid_m*BLOCK_M >= num_tokens_post_padded guard reads the device tensor and returns immediately. CORRECTNESS: asserted torch.equal on all three returned tensors against the ORIGINAL loop for T in {16,32,64,128} x block_m in {4,8,16,32} x 3 seeds (exact, including the pad value num_tokens*top_k in the oversized tail and stable-argsort ordering within each expert), plus a 60-iteration random interleaved-shape stress exercising 15 cached graphs. Harness: ALL CORRECTNESS CHECKS PASSED, err_ratio=0.0000 on all 4 cases. The graph cache is keyed on shape/dtype/block_m/num_experts only - never on tensor identity or content - and the real topk_ids are copied into the static input on every call, so every one of the 50 timed iterations does the full real work. MERGE: _moe_g1u1_fp8_kernel, its decorator and all tile-size defaults are byte-identical, so this should merge cleanly with the kernel-tiling engineer; block_m is a true runtime parameter and the graph cache is keyed on it, so a tile-size change just makes a different graph. REMAINING HEADROOM: post-patch the align step is only 1.7-2.5% of wall time; ~97% is now _moe_g1u1_fp8_kernel itself (case0 2.97 ms, case3 7.24 ms), so all further gains must come from the GEMM lane. CAVEAT: graph outputs live in the graph's private memory pool, so two align calls for the same shape alias the same buffers; safe here because the launcher consumes them in a stream-ordered kernel launch immediately after, but any future code that holds an align result across another same-shape align call must clone it. Benchmark reproduced twice: 5.1630 and 5.1642 ms geomean (0.02% spread).
